subject: environmental-science
title: Weather & Climate: Foundations
welcome_lead: Weather is what happens today; climate is the long-term pattern.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: weather vs climate, measurements.

concepts.def: How hot or cold the air is.
How much rain falls in an area.

walkthroughs.body_html: Weather changes hour by hour: sun, rain, wind, snow. Forecasts use models to predict the next few days.
Climate is the long-term average over decades. The UK climate is mild and wet. The Sahara climate is hot and dry.
Thermometers measure temperature, rain gauges measure rainfall, anemometers measure wind. Weather stations send data 24/7.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between ozone depletion and climate change?
options: Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Two distinct issues - ozone depletion is about UV protection (caused mainly by CFCs); climate change is about heat trapping (caused mainly by CO2).

mcqs.q: Why does renewable energy require energy storage solutions?
options: Solar and wind generation are intermittent - storage smooths out supply and demand.
Renewable energy can never meet demand.
Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Because they generate too much energy.

mcqs.q: Why is ice-albedo feedback a positive feedback loop?
options: Less ice means less reflective surface, so more sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming and more melting.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Because they generate too much energy.
Because warming is positive (a good thing).
